targetAudience.primary: Engineers and architects building resumable agent runtimes
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands persisted state, compaction, recovery and tool authorization.
targetAudience.readerProblem: A valid recovery snapshot can be mistaken for a current permission grant.

whyNow: A same-day merged OpenAI Codex change demonstrates context restoration from an eligible surviving full WorldState snapshot after nested-agent history transformation while rejecting partial and superseded state.

externalHook.description: A qualified full state baseline can restore continuity even when the originating task message no longer survives.

coreProposition: A durable snapshot may be authoritative enough to reconstruct context without being authoritative enough to authorize action; resumable Agent runtimes should keep reconstruction evidence, lineage and freshness identity, and current execution authorization separately inspectable, revalidating permission-bearing restored state before it can shape capabilities or effects.

originalValue.description: Separates evidence that authorizes reconstruction from current policy that authorizes action, with lineage and freshness retained as a separately inspectable identity.

readerTakeaway: Validate completeness and lineage to reconstruct context, then independently revalidate current authority before restored state can affect tools, credentials or external effects.

supported: An eligible surviving full WorldState snapshot can establish context continuity without counting as a user turn.
Bare TurnContext, patch-only state and compaction-superseded snapshots are rejected in the demonstrated tests.
Persisted and nested histories exercise restoration across serialization, forks and compaction.
unsupported: Current permission validity of every restored field
Universal cross-host or distributed recovery safety
uncertain: Which restored fields require fresh authorization
How generation identity should survive migrations

firstPartyRole.rationale: The argument is a general resumable-agent governance pattern and does not rely on a first-party project.

decisionReason: The implementation and negative tests support a concrete reconstruction boundary and a distinct, evidence-bounded governance interpretation.
